hypothesis.cheapest_refuting_observation: `@0x98 lhzu r0,38(r4)` (ours) against `@0x98 lhzu r0,38(r5)` (target) is a load-with-UPDATE in BOTH streams, so the cursor already exists as a compiler-built induction web in our object too; if `fnasm game/g3d/auxanim InitOAnimList 0x44:0xb0 --diff` after a cursor rewrite still shows `@0x38 li r6,0` on our side against `@0x38 li r3,0` on the target's, the renaming is downstream of the web's construction and no addressing form reaches it.

hypothesis.statement: The surviving loop-1 residual is a pure VOLATILE renaming that costs no callee-saved register, so it is separable from the save-set half. Every register named here is quoted with its defining instruction and stream offset, read from `fnasm game/g3d/auxanim InitOAnimList 0x30:0xb8 --diff` at commit a19fb90ba. The `off` accumulator: ours `@0x38 li r6,0` then `@0x50 addi r6,r6,40`; target `@0x38 li r3,0` then `@0x50 addi r3,r3,40`. The `p + off` base: ours `@0x44 add r4,r31,r6`; target `@0x44 add r5,r31,r3`. The untried construct class is the ADDRESS FORM of the inner accesses: our source spells them `*(u32*)(p + off + 0x20)` with a byte-offset accumulator, while the target's `@0x44 add r5,r31,r3` + `@0x48 lwz r0,32(r5)` + `@0x98 lhzu r0,38(r5)` sequence is a walked-pointer shape. Rewriting the loop against a walking `OANIM*` cursor (claim.law.sizeof-defeats-loop-stride-induction / the AddItemInstList index-form result) is the next lever.
